chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all together from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Whenever you love a man, inform him of that, for it will be an affirmation of the cordiality between the two of you.'

key_terms.أَثْبَتُ: athabatu: more affirming, more strengthening — the act of verbal expression makes the bond more stable and enduring
key_terms.الْمَوَدَّةِ: mawaddah: warm affection and cordiality between people, a deeper form of love that implies genuine care and goodwill

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq teach that you should tell someone when you love them?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that when a believer feels genuine love for his brother, he should express it openly and directly. This teaching reflects the Imam's emphasis on building transparent and strong bonds of brotherhood in the early Muslim community, where verbal affirmation of affection was understood as a spiritual and social virtue that deepens mutual trust and strengthens the ties of faith.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Bin Sali, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whenever you love a man, so inform him of that, for it would be an affirmation for the cordiality between the two of you’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Khalid and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“When you love a man, tell him about it; it strengthens your love for one another.”
